facts.fact: 又是楼梯、又是黑暗——但至少这一次她不是滚下来的，"不，这一次下降是我选的"
facts.anchor: More stairs. More darkness. At least I wasn’t falling down these ones. No, I was choosing this descent.

facts.fact: 她祈祷自己没疯；又自问："真疯了我会知道吗？"
facts.anchor: God, I hoped I wasn’t going mad. Would I even know?

facts.fact: 没有光，房间像在旋转，分不出上下，只是悬在空间里
facts.anchor: Without any light, the room felt as if it were spinning, no discernible up, no down. Just floating in space.

facts.fact: 那像她一直想象的死亡：无尽的黑暗、一个虚空，她独自在里面待到永远、无处可逃
facts.anchor: It was like what I’d always imagined death to be like. An unending darkness, a void, and me alone in it for all eternity with no escape.

facts.fact: 平时她会逃开这个——喝酒、漫无目的地换台、刷手机，做任何事躲开那种"可怕的无"
facts.anchor: Normally, I would run from this. I would drink or flick aimlessly through TV shows or scroll on my phone, anything to get away from the awful nothingness

facts.fact: 这一次她留在里面，尽管每根神经都叫她跑回楼上
facts.anchor: But this time I stayed in it, though every nerve told me to run back up the stairs

facts.fact: 然后她意识到这里有东西——"有恐惧"
facts.anchor: And then I realised there was something here. There was fear.

facts.fact: 她把恐惧当作一个"东西"紧紧抓住
facts.anchor: I held onto the fear as a something.

facts.fact: 她感觉胸腔起伏、心跳、衣服的移动——就像在山上林子里那样
facts.anchor: I felt the rise and fall of my chest, the beat of my heart, the shifting of my clothes—just like I had in the forestry on the hill.

facts.fact: 眼睛适应后，她看见了地下室，看见了那道门：淡淡的线，被灰泥抹过——"那道缺口"
facts.anchor: My eyes adjusted. And I saw the basement. And I saw the door. Faint lines, plastered over. The breach.

facts.fact: 她半以为门会被木板和钉子封死，但它和第一次看见时一样
facts.anchor: I’d half expected the door to be barricaded shut with planks and nails. But it was just like how I had seen it the first time.

facts.fact: "你在干什么？劈还是剁？"——这是她刚搬来时、需要人帮忙看锅炉，Rowan 问她的
facts.anchor: “What are you doing? Splitting or chopping?”

facts.fact: 她举斧时是出于愤怒与恐惧，把一样东西砍成了两样："斧头能把两样东西砍回一样吗？"
facts.anchor: When I’d raised my axe in wrath, in fear, I’d hacked one thing into two. Could an axe ever cut two things back into one?

facts.fact: 她想到：把两样东西砍成一样，完全可能
facts.anchor: It occurred to me that it was entirely possible to chop two things into one.

facts.fact: 那句问话又响起；她心里答"剁"，一斧劈进门板
facts.anchor: “What are you doing? Splitting or chopping?” Chopping, I answered and swung my axe into the door.

facts.fact: 这一次破坏是有条理的：肾上腺素更少，精确更多
facts.anchor: The destruction was organised this time. Less adrenaline, more precision.

facts.fact: 每一击都像鼓点
facts.anchor: Each hit sounded like the beat of a drum.

facts.fact: 她节奏稳定，像节拍器一样挥动，拆掉挡路的障碍，把两座房子合到一起，让它们重新成为一个家
facts.anchor: I had a good steady rhythm, swinging like a metronome, breaking down the barrier in my way, bringing the houses together, making them one home once more.

facts.fact: 突然，光从渐渐变大的缺口里涌进来
facts.anchor: Suddenly, light poured through the growing gap.

facts.fact: 她努力不去想那些光是从哪儿来的
facts.anchor: I tried not to think about where all the light was coming from.

facts.fact: 她把斧头穿过缺口，用它撬开、扯下长条薄板
facts.anchor: I pushed the axe through the breach and used it to lever and rip away long thin panels.

facts.fact: 她侧肩撞开缝隙挤了过去——"进了我邻居的家。"
facts.anchor: Into my neighbour’s house.
